question.text: Post-listing, in addition to the financial (by October 31 / IT-return due date) and non-financial (60-day) annual disclosures under LODR Chapter IX-A, which of the following is CORRECT?

answer.text: The Social Stock Exchange(s) MAY specify matters that shall be disclosed by the NPO on an annual basis, in addition to SEBI-prescribed disclosures.
SSE cannot specify any additional disclosures beyond SEBI's list.
Only the Ministry of Corporate Affairs can prescribe additional disclosures.
NPOs are exempt from all post-listing disclosures once registered.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 3.2 (Disclosures by NPO, sub-point 2) states: 'In addition to the disclosures referred in sub-regulation (1), the Social Stock Exchange(s) may specify matters that shall be disclosed by the Not for Profit Organization on an annual basis.' The SSE has delegated power to add matters — the SIA must track SSE circulars, not just SEBI circulars. The Trap: Option A misreads the regulation as exclusive. Option C inserts MCA falsely. Option D wrongly exempts NPOs. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C (Compliance) covers both SEBI and exchange-level disclosure obligations. The 'stock-exchange-may-add' principle is common across LODR (Reg 30 Part B). XV (RA) reads both sets. XXIII puts it in the SSE context. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Maintain a 'Disclosure Source Map' with columns: SEBI circular, SSE circular, LODR chapter, effective date, SIA-touch-point. When SSE issues a new disclosure circular (they do periodically since the 2022 and 2023 framework updates), map it into the audit plan for the NEXT annual cycle.
